text.p: VIENNA, July 14 (Reuter) The main stories in the Austrian press this Monday are:

- President Thomas Klestil says that staying out of NATO could have fatal consequences and urges the Social Democrats and conservative People's Party to clarify their positions on Austria's security policy.
- Two men who threatened to poison food of grocery chain Meinl unless they received a 25 million schilling ransom are in custody.
- Klestil is in favour of Austria's joining NATO, but sees it as unlikely to happen before the turn of the century.
- President Thomas Klestil says he believes that the coalition government will hold until 1999.
- Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger contracts out railway funding to help meet the Maastricht budget deficit criteria.
- Austria's conservative People's Party should take a stronger stand for the underprivileged and have more party discipline, according to a poll
- President Thomas Klestil wants an open debate over possible Austrian entry to NATO and warns of the disadvantages of staying out of international security structures.
- Austria's energy industry is in a tug of war over the best position once the market is liberalised.
- State Secretary Wolfgang Ruttenstorfer says tough negotiations are necessary on the pension reforms for the civil service. These must be completed by the beginning of September.
- Machine maker Emco faces a decisive week over whether bankrupcy can be avoided any longer.
